sealed_record.thesis: Structural memory (DRAM/HBM) shortage thesis converging from multiple independent voices. Meritz's Kim Sunwoo (via aleabitoreddit) argues the market misunderstands semis: H2 2026 suppliers can fulfill only 75-80% of DRAM demand, falling into the 60% range by 2027, with Intel's CEO quoted saying 'no relief in memory supply or pricing until at least 2028.' jukan05 corroborates independently: HBM-dedicated line buildouts in H1 sharply cut absolute commodity DRAM (DDR5/LPDDR5X) capacity, shifting pricing power decisively from set-makers to memory manufacturers as the shortage spreads to commodity DRAM. MU's take-or-pay LTAs point to durable structural demand. Yet SK Hynix trades at ~3.5x 2027 P/E and Samsung ~3.9x - deeply mispriced for a multi-year supply shortage. Long the cheapest structural-shortage beneficiary.
